story_text.value:
137 file types; a single file with nothing to install. Introducing Provost, the free compression and archival tool that can create 119 formats, and open 137 total. It's new custom format packs smaller than ZPAQ, xz, and Zstandard in tests. JPEG, PNG, PDF, DOCX/XLSX, and gzip are unpacked and repacked for ~25% smaller files; ability to encrypt to people's keys or a password; can open archives straight from HTTPS, S3, WebDAV, and SFTP; can search inside archives, including the text of Office files and PDFs; and much more.

Q&A --- Is it open source? It is not.

Will my .provost files open in five years? I've committed to future releases reading every 0.1.0 archive, and to old compression methods staying readable.

Are builds signed? No. The Mac app isn't notarized and the Windows exes are unsigned, so you will see Gatekeeper and SmartScreen warnings.

Is the .exe an installer? Nope; it's a stand-alone executable. This is true for all GUI and CLI builds across all three OSes.

Is the custom .provost compression fast? Levels 7 to 9 are very slow. There is a built-in benchmark test.

How was it built? AI.

title.value: Show HN: Archiver that opens every format

story_text.value:
Hi, a while ago I made Zpup, small library that inspired by Zdog. I kept working on it, and it grew in to nice tool for making 3D scenes.

The link is small game drawn with it.

Image models cant draw the same thing twice. but Zpup solves this with simple way. the model writes small 3D scene as JSON, Zpup draws it from any angle. the objects are written once, so it looks same in every direction.

I wrote the game rules by hand. the resources are simple. they will not look better than image models. because it is not 3D engine.

Repo (MIT): https://github.com/rxolve/zpup

title.value: Show HN: Zpup – tiny 3D scene format made for LLMs to write
